verdict.rationale: SerpApi documents a U.S. Legal Shield that covers scraping and parsing of search engine data as long as the customer's use is not illegal, with up to $2M coverage on Production plans and above. A community post quotes it as protecting the right to crawl public search data under the First Amendment. Together these form a documented legal stance on permitted use, but only a thin one. Missing for 10: any documented robots.txt policy, any content licensing or copyright stance on returned results, and explicit permitted-use terms beyond 'not illegal'.
